claims.claim: The Didache is an anonymous early Christian treatise; its author is unknown and it is attributed to no specific individual, though it presents itself as the teaching of the twelve apostles.
The Didache was written in Koine Greek, probably in Egypt or Syria, with Syria and Palestine being the most favored locations.
The work was written as a community manual for scattered rural Christian communities, giving advice on practical subjects including Christian ethics, rituals, and church organization.
The Didache presents itself as 'The Teaching of the Lord, through the Twelve Apostles, to the Gentiles' or 'Nations,' suggesting it was conceived for Gentile converts.

The treatise deals with three main areas: the 'Two Ways' (Way of Life and Way of Death), rituals including baptism, fasting, and Eucharist, and church organization including itinerant apostles, prophets, bishops, and deacons.

The Didache survives primarily through a Greek manuscript written in 1056 CE, discovered in 1873 by Philotheos Bryennios, Greek Orthodox metropolitan of Nicomedia, in a codex in Constantinople (Istanbul); this manuscript is kept in Jerusalem.
An old Latin translation of chapters 1-5 was found by Dr. J. Schlecht in 1900.
The Didache is considered the oldest surviving Christian church order and the first example of the genre, making it significant for understanding primitive Christianity.
The Didache is considered a product of the group of second-generation Christian writers known as the Apostolic Fathers.
